info.description: REST API of ONLYOFFICE DocSpace - a multi-tenant platform for document management, collaboration and file sharing. Requests are authenticated with the portal session cookie, an API key, Basic credentials, or an OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect token; see the security schemes of this document.

post.description:
Creates an API key that authenticates requests as the caller.
Any signed-in user can call it, except a guest. A guest gets 403.
If the portal limits developer tools to DocSpace admins, other callers also get 403.
The call changes data. Do not repeat it. Each call creates a new key.
The response has the full secret in `key`. No other call returns it, so store it now.
Send it in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer sk-...`.
Pass `*` or leave out `permissions` to create a key without scope restrictions.
By default, the limit is 5 calls in 15 minutes per user. More calls return 429.
The call returns 400 if `name` is missing, empty, or too long, or if `expiresInDays` is out of range.
It also returns 400 if `permissions` is empty or has an unknown scope.

schema.description: The request parameters for creating a new API key.

200.description: The new API key, with the full secret in the key field

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Rate limit: 5 requests per 15 minutes per user/IP.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests remaining in the current 15-minute window.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the current 15-minute window resets.

400.description: The request body cannot be read or has no `name`, the name is empty or longer than 30 characters, `expiresInDays` is outside 1-365, or the permissions array is empty or contains a scope the portal does not know

403.description: The caller is a guest, or the portal limits developer tools to administrators

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying (5 req / 15 min limit per user/IP).

get.description:
Returns the API keys that the caller can see.
A DocSpace admin gets every key of the portal. Other users get only the keys they created.
Any signed-in user can call it, except a guest. A guest gets 403.
The call is read-only.
The list includes expired and deactivated keys, so check `expiresAt` and `isActive`.
For a user, an empty list means they created no keys, not that the portal has none.

200.description: Every key of the portal for a DocSpace admin, or the keys created by the caller for anybody else

403.description: The caller is a guest

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns every scope that the `permissions` array of an API key accepts.
Use these values in `POST api/2.0/keys` and `PUT api/2.0/keys/{keyId}`.
Those calls accept no other value.
Any signed-in user can call it, except a guest. A guest gets 403.
The call is read-only.
The list is in alphabetical order and the same for every caller.
Besides the scopes of each area, it has `*:read`, `*:write`, and `*`.
The value `*` means a key without scope restrictions.

200.description: The scope values accepted in the permissions array of an API key

403.description: The caller is a guest

get.description:
Returns the API key that authenticated this request.
So a key holder can read its scopes, expiry, and state without knowing its ID.
Send the key in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer sk-...`.
Any key can call it, whatever its scopes.
If the request uses a cookie or a user token, the call returns 400.
The call is read-only.
To read other keys, use `GET api/2.0/keys`.

200.description: The API key that authenticated this request

400.description: The request is not authenticated by an API key, as with a session authenticated by a cookie or by a user token

put.description:
Renames an API key, replaces its scopes, or turns it on or off. The secret stays the same.
Requires the creator of the key or a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403.
The call changes data. You can repeat it with the same body.
It changes only the fields in the body.
Pass only `*` in `permissions` to remove all scope restrictions.
With `isActive` set to false, the key stops authenticating requests but stays in the list.
The call returns `true` after a change.
For an expired key, it changes nothing and returns `false`.
To remove a key for good, use `DELETE api/2.0/keys/{keyId}`.
If no key has this ID, the call returns 404.
The call returns 400 if the name is empty, has only spaces, or is too long.
It also returns 400 if `permissions` is empty or has an unknown scope.

parameters.name: keyId
parameters.description:
The ID of the key to update, taken from the route. Read it from the `id` of an entry of
`GET api/2.0/keys` - it is not the secret and not the `keyPostfix`.

requestBody.description:
The fields to change. Every field is optional and the ones that are left out keep their current values, so an
empty object changes nothing.

schema.description:

200.description: True if the key was changed, false if it was left untouched because it has already expired

403.description: The key belongs to another member and the caller is not a DocSpace admin

delete.description:
Deletes an API key. The key stops authenticating requests immediately.
Requires the creator of the key or a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403.
The call cannot be undone, and a repeated call returns 404.
It always returns `true`.
To stop a key for a time, set `isActive` to false with `PUT api/2.0/keys/{keyId}`.
To get a new key, use `POST api/2.0/keys`.
If no key has this ID, the call returns 404.

parameters.description:
The ID of the key to delete, taken from the route. Read it from the `id` of an entry of
`GET api/2.0/keys` - it is not the secret and not the `keyPostfix`.

200.description: True if the key was removed

get.description:
Returns the groups of the portal, one page at a time. Each entry has the ID, the name, and the manager, but no
members. Requires a DocSpace admin or a room admin. Other callers get 403. The call is read-only. The
response reports the total number of matching groups, so you can page with `count` and `startIndex`. The
call matches `filterValue` against any part of the group name and ignores case. With `userId`, it keeps only
the groups of that account. With `manager` set to true, it keeps only the groups that account manages. An
unknown `sortBy` value orders the groups by title. The call returns 400 if `count` is out of range or a
parameter has the wrong type. To read the members of one group, use `GET api/2.0/group/{id}`.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Keeps only the groups the account with this ID takes part in. Omit it to search every group of the portal.

parameters.name: manager
parameters.description:
Narrows `userId` down to the groups that account manages, instead of every group it belongs to. It has no
effect on its own and defaults to false.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The size of the page. It defaults to 100, which is also the largest value the operation accepts.

parameters.name: startIndex
parameters.description:
The number of matching groups to skip before the page starts. It defaults to 0, and the total number of
matches is reported in the total count of the response.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description:
What to order the groups by: `Title`, `Manager` or `MembersCount`, compared without regard to case. Any other
value, and omitting the field, orders by title.

parameters.name: sortOrder
parameters.description: The direction of the ordering: `Ascending`, which is the default, or `Descending`.

parameters.name: filterValue
parameters.description: The text to match against the group name. Omit it to get every group.

200.description: The matching groups, with their summary information

400.description: A parameter has the wrong type, or the `count` is outside its allowed range

403.description: No permissions to perform this action

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Creates a group with a name and, optionally, a manager and members. The manager also becomes a member.
Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. A room admin can read groups but also gets 403 here. The
call changes data. Do not repeat it. Group names are not unique, so each call creates another group. The
response is the new group with its members. The call returns 400 if the name is missing, blank, or too long.
It also returns 400 if the manager or any member is a guest, a disabled account, or an unknown ID. In that
case, the call creates nothing.

Raises the `group.created` webhook once for the new group. It does not raise `user.*` webhooks for the manager or the members.

schema.description: The group request parameters.

200.description: The new group, with its members

400.description: The request body cannot be read or has no `groupName`, the group name is `null`, blank or longer than 128 characters, or one of the listed members or the manager is a guest, is disabled or does not exist

403.description: No permissions to perform this action

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

x-docspace-webhooks.when: once for the new group. It does not raise `user.*` webhooks for the manager or the members

get.description:
Returns one group by its ID, with its name, its manager, and its members. Requires a DocSpace admin or a room
admin. Other callers get 403. The call is read-only. Set `includeMembers` to false to leave out the members
of a large group. If no group has this ID or the group is deleted, the call returns 404. To find a group by
name, use `GET api/2.0/group`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The ID of the group to read, taken from the route. It has to be a group that has not been deleted, otherwise
the operation answers 404.

parameters.name: includeMembers
parameters.description:
Whether to fill in the member list of the group. It defaults to true, so set it to false when only the name
and the manager are needed and the group may be large.

200.description: The group, with its members when includeMembers was set

403.description: No permissions to perform this action

404.description: No group has the specified ID

400.description: Bad Request.

put.description:
Changes the name and the manager of a group, and adds or removes members, in one call. Requires a DocSpace
admin. Other callers get 403. A room admin can read groups but also gets 403 here. The call changes data.
You can repeat it with the same body. A field that you leave out keeps its current value. This call cannot
remove the manager. It skips a guest, a disabled account, or an unknown ID in `groupManager` and
`membersToAdd`. It also skips an ID in `membersToRemove` that is not a member. The call adds members first
and then removes them. So an account in both lists ends up removed. The response is the group after the
update. Compare it with the request to see what the call skipped. If no group has this ID, the call
returns 404. The call returns 400 if `groupName` is too long.

Raises the `group.updated` webhook only when the name, the manager, or the members change. It does not raise `user.*` webhooks for those accounts.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The ID of the group to update, taken from the route. It has to be a group that has not been deleted,
otherwise the operation answers 404.

requestBody.description:
The fields to change. Every field is optional and the ones that are left out keep their current values, so an
empty object changes nothing.

schema.description:
The fields to change. Every field is optional and the ones that are left out keep their current values, so an
empty object changes nothing.

200.description: The group as it is after the update

400.description: The request body cannot be read, or `groupName` is longer than 128 characters

404.description: No group has the specified ID

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

x-docspace-webhooks.when: only when the name, the manager, or the members change. It does not raise `user.*` webhooks for those accounts

delete.description:
Deletes a group and removes its access to rooms, folders, and files. Members who had access only through the
group lose it. The call keeps the accounts of the members. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403.
The deletion cannot be undone. A repeated call returns 404. The call returns 204 with no body. If no group
has this ID, the call returns 404. To empty a group without deleting it, use
`DELETE api/2.0/group/{id}/members`.

Raises the `group.deleted` webhook once for the deleted group. It does not raise `user.*` webhooks for its former members.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The ID of the group to delete, taken from the route. It has to be a group that has not been deleted already,
otherwise the operation answers 404.

204.description: The group is deleted. No content is returned

403.description: No permissions to perform this action

404.description: No group has the specified ID

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

x-docspace-webhooks.when: once for the deleted group. It does not raise `user.*` webhooks for its former members

get.description:
Returns all groups that an account belongs to, as ID and name pairs. Requires a DocSpace admin or a room
admin. Other callers get 403, even for their own groups. The call is read-only and does not page the list.
The entries have no manager and no members. An empty list means the account is in no group or does not
exist. To read one group in full, use `GET api/2.0/group/{id}`.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description:
The ID of the account whose groups are listed, taken from the route. An ID that matches no account yields an
empty list rather than 404.

200.description: The groups the account belongs to, as ID and name pairs

403.description: No permissions to perform this action

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

put.description:
Moves the members of one group to another group. The source group stays, without these members. Requires a
DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. A room admin can read groups but also gets 403 here. The call changes
data, and you can repeat it. If both IDs are the same, the call changes nothing. The destination group keeps
its manager. If the manager of the source group leaves it, the source group has no manager after the call.
The call skips disabled members, so they stay in the source group. A guest member leaves the source group
but does not join the destination. The response is the destination group with its members. If no group has
one of the IDs, the call returns 404. To move only some members, use `PUT api/2.0/group/{id}/members` and
`DELETE api/2.0/group/{id}/members`. To delete the source group, use `DELETE api/2.0/group/{id}`.

Raises the `group.updated` webhook for the source group if the two IDs differ and the source has enabled members. Raises the `group.updated` webhook for the destination group only when its members change. It does not raise `user.*` webhooks for the moved members.

parameters.name: fromId
parameters.description:
The ID of the group the members are taken from. It is emptied but not deleted, and it has to be a group that
has not been deleted already.

parameters.name: toId
parameters.description:
The ID of the group the members are moved into. It is the group the answer describes, and it has to be a
group that has not been deleted already.

200.description: The destination group with its members

403.description: No permissions to perform this action

404.description: No group has one of the specified IDs

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

x-docspace-webhooks.when: for the source group if the two IDs differ and the source has enabled members
for the destination group only when its members change. It does not raise `user.*` webhooks for the moved members

post.description:
Replaces the members of a group with the listed accounts. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. A
room admin can read groups but also gets 403 here. The call changes data. You can repeat it with the same
body. First, the call removes the current members, except disabled ones. Then it adds the listed accounts. It
skips a guest, a disabled account, or an unknown ID. These two steps are not atomic. So a failure between
them can leave the group empty. The response is the group with the members it ends up with. If no group has
this ID, the call returns 404. The call returns 400 if the list is missing, empty, or has no account that can
be a member. In that case, the group does not change. To add or remove a few accounts, use
`PUT api/2.0/group/{id}/members` or `DELETE api/2.0/group/{id}/members`.

Raises the `group.updated` webhook only when the members or the manager change. It does not raise `user.*` webhooks for the added or removed members.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The ID of the group whose members are changed, taken from the route. It has to be a group that has not been
deleted, otherwise the operation answers 404.

requestBody.description: The accounts to add, replace with, or remove.

schema.description: The accounts to add, replace with, or remove.

200.description: The group with the members it ends up with

400.description: The request body cannot be read or has no `members` list, or none of the listed accounts can be a group member

403.description: No permissions to perform this action

404.description: No group has the specified ID

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

x-docspace-webhooks.when: only when the members or the manager change. It does not raise `user.*` webhooks for the added or removed members

put.description:
Adds the listed accounts to a group and keeps its current members. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers
get 403. A room admin can read groups but also gets 403 here. The call changes data. You can repeat it with
the same body. The call skips a guest, a disabled account, an unknown ID, and a current member. An empty list
changes nothing. The response is the group with its members after the call. If no group has this ID, the call
returns 404. This call does not change the manager. To set the manager, use
`PUT api/2.0/group/{id}/manager`. To replace all members, use `POST api/2.0/group/{id}/members`.

Raises the `group.updated` webhook only when the call adds at least one account. It does not raise `user.*` webhooks for the added members.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The ID of the group whose members are changed, taken from the route. It has to be a group that has not been
deleted, otherwise the operation answers 404.

requestBody.description: The accounts to add, replace with, or remove.

schema.description: The accounts to add, replace with, or remove.

200.description: The group with its members after the addition

403.description: No permissions to perform this action

404.description: No group has the specified ID

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

x-docspace-webhooks.when: only when the call adds at least one account. It does not raise `user.*` webhooks for the added members

delete.description:
Removes the listed accounts from a group and keeps the other members. The accounts stay, but they lose the
access they had through the group. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. A room admin can read
groups but also gets 403 here. The call changes data. You can repeat it with the same body. The call skips
an ID that is not a member or matches no account. An empty list changes nothing. The response is the group
with the remaining members. If no group has this ID, the call returns 404. To remove all members, list them
all here.

Raises the `group.updated` webhook only when the call removes at least one member. It does not raise `user.*` webhooks for the removed members.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The ID of the group whose members are changed, taken from the route. It has to be a group that has not been
deleted, otherwise the operation answers 404.

requestBody.description: The accounts to add, replace with, or remove.

schema.description: The accounts to add, replace with, or remove.

200.description: The group with the members that remain

403.description: No permissions to perform this action

404.description: No group has the specified ID

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

x-docspace-webhooks.when: only when the call removes at least one member. It does not raise `user.*` webhooks for the removed members

put.description:
Makes an account the manager of a group and replaces the previous manager. The account also becomes a member.
The previous manager stays a member. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. A room admin can read
groups but also gets 403 here. The call changes data. You can repeat it with the same body. If the account is
a guest or disabled, the call changes nothing. The response is the group with its manager. The call returns
404 if no group has this ID or no account has `userId`. It also returns 400 if `userId` is missing. To
change the members, use `PUT api/2.0/group/{id}/members`.

Raises the `group.updated` webhook only when the manager or the members change. It does not raise `user.*` webhooks for the new or previous manager.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The ID of the group whose manager is set, taken from the route. It has to be a group that has not been
deleted, otherwise the operation answers 404.

requestBody.description: The account to make the manager of the group.

schema.description: The account to make the manager of the group.

200.description: The group with its new manager

400.description: The request body cannot be read or has no `userId`

403.description: No permissions to perform this action

404.description: No group has the specified ID, or no account has the specified userId

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

x-docspace-webhooks.when: only when the manager or the members change. It does not raise `user.*` webhooks for the new or previous manager

get.description:
Returns the portal groups for sharing the room. The `shared` field tells whether a group already has access.
The list also has the system group Everyone. Requires the right to change access to the room. Other callers
get 403. If no room has the ID, the call returns 404. The call is read-only. It sorts the groups by name and
pages them by `count` and `startIndex`, with a total count. An empty `filterValue` returns every group.
Otherwise, the call keeps the groups whose name contains the value, in any case. With `excludeShared`, the
call returns only the groups without access. The call returns 400 if `count` is outside 1 to 100. To search
users and groups together, use `GET api/2.0/accounts/room/{id}/search`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The ID of the room, folder or file whose access the search is run against, taken from the route. It is an
integer for an entry stored in DocSpace and a provider-specific string for an entry in a connected
third-party storage.

parameters.name: excludeShared
parameters.description:
Keeps only the groups that do not have access to the entry yet, which is the set to offer when granting
access. Every returned entry then has `shared` set to false; without the flag every matching group comes back
and `shared` tells them apart.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The size of the page. It defaults to 100, which is also the largest value the operation accepts.

parameters.name: startIndex
parameters.description:
The number of matching groups to skip before the page starts. It defaults to 0, and the total number of
matches is reported in the total count of the response.

parameters.name: filterValue
parameters.description: The text to match against the group name. Omit it to get every group the caller may grant access to.

200.description: The matching groups, each with its access state for the room

400.description: A parameter has the wrong type, or the `count` is outside its allowed range

403.description: No permissions to perform this action

404.description: No room has the specified ID

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The ID of the room, folder or file whose access the search is run against, taken from the route. It is an
integer for an entry stored in DocSpace and a provider-specific string for an entry in a connected
third-party storage.

malformed or punycode address, or for the address of a disabled account. The call handles the addresses in

that the caller can see, not only the new ones. The portal limits the rate of these calls. To send an invitation
again, use `PUT api/2.0/people/invite`.

or contacts. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403, including a room admin. The call is read-only. It
matches the term as a substring and ignores case. If `query` is missing, the call returns 400. With `filterBy`
set to `group`, `filterValue` is a group ID. The call then keeps only the members of that group. The list has no
paging, no total, and no fixed order. For a page with a total, use `GET api/2.0/people/filter`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
The account state to search in, taken from the route: `Active` for working accounts, `Terminated` for
disabled ones, `Pending` for open invitations, or `All` for every state.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description:
The term to look for, matched as a case-insensitive substring of the first name, the last name, the user
name, the email and the contacts. It is required in practice, because the search cannot run without it.

parameters.name: filterBy
parameters.description:
The only recognised value is `group`, which turns `filterValue` into a group ID and keeps only the members of
that group. Any other value, and omitting the field, applies no group filter.

parameters.name: filterValue
parameters.description:
The group ID to keep the members of, used only when `filterBy` is `group`. It has to be a valid identifier -
a group name is not accepted.

200.description: The full profiles of the matching accounts

400.description: A parameter has the wrong type, or `query` is missing

403.description: The caller is not a DocSpace administrator

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns a page of the accounts that match all the given filters, with full profiles. Requires a room admin, a
DocSpace admin, or an admin of the People module. Other callers get 403. A DocSpace admin sees more accounts
than a room admin. The call is read-only and works on an unpaid portal. The response has the total number of
matches. If `count` is out of range, the call returns 400. If both are set, `employeeType` wins over
`employeeTypes`. With `withoutGroup`, the call ignores `groupId`. The `area` filter cancels the type filters
that contradict it. For short profiles with the same filters, use `GET api/2.0/people/simple/filter`.

parameters.name: employeeStatus
parameters.description:
Keeps only the accounts in the given state: `Active` for working accounts, `Terminated` for disabled ones
and `Pending` for open invitations. Omit it to search every state.

parameters.name: groupId
parameters.description:
Keeps only the members of this group, or excludes them when `excludeGroup` is true. It is ignored when
`withoutGroup` is set.

parameters.name: activationStatus
parameters.description:
Keeps only the accounts whose activation is in the given state: `NotActivated`, `Activated`, `Pending` or
`AutoGenerated`. Omit it to search every state.

parameters.name: employeeType
parameters.description:
Keeps only the accounts of this single type: `DocSpaceAdmin`, `RoomAdmin`, `User` or `Guest`. When it is
sent it wins over `employeeTypes`, and a type that contradicts `area` is dropped.

parameters.name: employeeTypes
parameters.description:
Keeps the accounts of any of the listed types, combined as alternatives. It is ignored when `employeeType`
is also sent.

anyOf.description: [All - All, RoomAdmin - Room admin, Guest - Guest, DocSpaceAdmin - DocSpace admin, User - User]
[0 - All, 1 - Room admin, 2 - Guest, 3 - DocSpace admin, 4 - User]

parameters.name: isAdministrator
parameters.description:
Set it to true to keep only the DocSpace administrators and the module administrators. Setting it to false
is the same as omitting it and does not exclude administrators.

parameters.name: payments
parameters.description:
Keeps only the accounts that take a paid seat when `Paid`, or only the guests and members that do not when
`Free`. Omit it to search both.

parameters.name: accountLoginType
parameters.description:
Keeps only the accounts that sign in this way: `SSO`, `LDAP`, or `Standart` for an ordinary portal
password. Omit it to search all of them.

parameters.name: quotaFilter
parameters.description:
Keeps only the accounts whose storage quota is the portal default when `Default`, or set individually when
`Custom`. `All`, which is the same as omitting the field, searches both.

parameters.name: withoutGroup
parameters.description:
Set it to true to keep only the accounts that belong to no group at all, which makes `groupId` and
`excludeGroup` irrelevant.

parameters.name: excludeGroup
parameters.description:
Inverts `groupId`: with true the members of that group are left out instead of being the only ones kept. It
has no effect without `groupId`.

parameters.name: invitedByMe
parameters.description:
Keeps only the accounts invited by the caller when true, and only those invited by somebody else when
false. Omit it to search regardless of who sent the invitation.

parameters.name: inviterId
parameters.description:
Keeps only the accounts invited by the account with this ID. Omit it to search regardless of who sent the
invitation.

parameters.name: area
parameters.description:
The part of the portal to search in: `All`, the default, searches members and guests together, `People`
leaves the guests out, and `Guests` returns guests only. It also cancels the type filters that contradict
it.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The size of the page. It defaults to 100, which is also the largest value the operation accepts.

parameters.name: startIndex
parameters.description:
The number of matches to skip before the page starts. It defaults to 0, and the total number of matches is
reported in the total count of the response.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description:
What to order the accounts by, compared without regard to case: `FirstName`, `LastName`, `DisplayName`,
`Type`, `Email`, `Department`, `UsedSpace`, `CreatedBy` or `RegistrationDate`.

parameters.name: sortOrder
parameters.description: The direction of the ordering: `Ascending`, which is the default, or `Descending`.

parameters.name: filterSeparator
parameters.description:
The character that splits `filterValue` into several terms, of which any one may match. Omit it to split
the value on spaces instead, in which case every term has to match.

parameters.name: filterValue
parameters.description:
The text to match against the first name, the last name and the email, case-insensitively. Omit it to apply
no text filter at all.

400.description: A parameter has the wrong type, or the `count` is outside its allowed range

403.description: The caller is a member or a guest

get.description:
Returns the portal accounts that match a search, with whether each one has access to the room. Any signed-in user
with read access to the room can call it, except a guest. Other callers get 403. If no room has the ID, the call
returns 404. The call is read-only. If `filterValue` is empty, it returns every account that matches the other
filters. With `excludeShared`, the call returns only accounts without access. With `includeShared`, it returns
only accounts with access. If both are set, `excludeShared` wins. Without them, the `shared` field of each profile
shows the access. The call does not sort the list. The `count` and `startIndex` parameters page over it, and
`total` counts all matches. A caller who is not a DocSpace admin sees only the guests related to them. With `area`
set to `All`, they also see guests with access. If `count` is out of range, the call returns 400. To search users
and groups together, use `GET api/2.0/accounts/room/{id}/search`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The ID of the room, folder or file the search is run against, taken from the route. It is an integer for an
entry stored in DocSpace and a provider-specific string for an entry in a connected third-party storage.

parameters.name: employeeStatus
parameters.description:
Keeps only the accounts in the given state: `Active` for working accounts, `Terminated` for disabled ones
and `Pending` for open invitations. Omit it to search every state.

parameters.name: activationStatus
parameters.description:
Keeps only the accounts whose activation is in the given state: `NotActivated`, `Activated`, `Pending` or
`AutoGenerated`. Omit it to search every state.

parameters.name: excludeShared
parameters.description:
Keeps only the accounts that do not have access to the entry yet, which is the set to offer when granting
access. It takes precedence over `includeShared`, and every returned entry has `shared` set to false.

parameters.name: includeShared
parameters.description:
Keeps only the accounts that already have access to the entry, which is the set to offer when changing or
revoking access. Every returned entry has `shared` set to true, and the flag is ignored when `excludeShared`
is also set.

account, not to the portal. Any signed-in user can call it, including a guest. The call is read-only. If the

Changes the interface theme of the caller to `Base`, `Dark`, or `System`. The theme belongs to the account, not
to the portal. Any signed-in user can call it, including a guest. The call changes data. You can repeat it with
the same body. It returns the saved theme. If the body has no `theme`, the call returns 400. The `theme` field
of `GET api/2.0/people/@self` has the same value.

get.description:
Returns the third-party identity providers that the portal has turned on. Each item has the URL that starts
sign-in with that provider. Anyone can call it without signing in. The call is read-only. An empty list means
that the portal has no provider turned on. The `linked` field shows if the provider is linked to the account
of the caller. For an anonymous caller, `linked` is always false. The portal sets the order, but a caller in
China gets `weixin` first. If `fromOnly` is set, the call keeps only that provider. The value `openid`
selects `google`. With `inviteView`, the call leaves out the providers that cannot accept an invitation. With
`settingsView` or `inviteView`, the URLs always open in a popup. Otherwise, a URL redirects only for a mobile
browser or the desktop app. To link a provider to your account, use
`PUT api/2.0/people/thirdparty/linkaccount`. To create an account through a provider, use
`POST api/2.0/people/thirdparty/signup`.

parameters.name: inviteView
parameters.description:
Set it to true when the list is rendered on an invitation page: the providers that cannot be used to accept an
invitation, `twitter` and `appleid`, are then left out. It defaults to false, which returns every enabled
provider.

parameters.name: settingsView

Returns the state of the type change job of an account. Start the job with `POST api/2.0/people/type`. Requires
a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. A room admin also gets 403, even for its own job. The call is
read-only. This is the call to poll. Repeat it until `isCompleted` is true. If no job exists for the account,
the call returns 200 with an empty body. A failed job has its message in `error`. To cancel a running job, use
`PUT api/2.0/people/type/terminate`.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description:
The ID of the user the operation applies to, taken from the route. For a progress operation it has to be the
same ID that was passed when the job was started.

200.description: The state of the queued user type change, or an empty body when nothing is queued for the user

403.description: No permissions to perform this action

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

put.description:
Cancels the type change job of an account. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call changes
data, and you can repeat it. If no job exists for the account, the call returns 200 with an empty body.
Cancelling does not undo the type change or the moves that the job already made. You cannot resume a cancelled
job. To try again, start a new job with `POST api/2.0/people/type`. The response has `status` set to `Canceled`
and `isCompleted` set to true. If `userId` is missing, the call returns 400.

schema.description:
The request parameters that address the queued job of a single user - a data reassignment, a data deletion or a
user type change.

200.description: The state of the cancelled user type change, or an empty body when nothing was queued for the user

400.description: The request body cannot be read or has no `userId`

get.description:
Returns a link that lets another admin add a guest of the caller to their own guest list. Any signed-in user can
call it, except a guest. A guest gets 403. If the caller cannot see the account, the call also returns 403. If
the account is not a guest, the call returns 400. If no account has the ID, the call returns 404. The call is
read-only. It returns a short confirmation link. Give it to the room admin or DocSpace admin who should get the
guest. They accept it with `POST api/2.0/people/guests/share/approve`. The link has a token that expires, so
create it right before use.

password.description:
The password in plain text. It is checked against the portal password policy and rejected with 400 when it is
too weak. When neither this field nor `passwordHash` is sent, a random password is generated and nobody
learns it, so the account can only be used after a password recovery.

passwordHash.description:
The password already hashed by the client, which is what the portal stores. It is a PBKDF2-HMACSHA256 hash of
the plain password, computed with the salt, the iteration count and the key size the portal settings publish,
and written as lowercase hexadecimal. When it is sent, `password` is ignored and the password policy is not
applied.

email.description:
The email address of the new account, up to 255 characters. It is required in practice and has to be a real
address, and it becomes the sign-in name of the account.

type.description:
The type of the new account: `User`, `RoomAdmin` or `DocSpaceAdmin`. `Guest` is not accepted here, and the
value is ignored entirely when `fromInviteLink` is set, because the invitation link decides the type. When no
paid seat is free, the account is created as `User` whatever was asked for.

isUser.description:
Only chooses which entry the operation writes to the audit trail - the one for a guest or the one for a
member. It does not change the type of the account; `type` and the invitation link do that.

firstName.description:
The first name, up to 255 characters. It is checked together with `lastName`, and a pair the portal does not
accept as a name answers 400.

lastName.description:
The last name, up to 255 characters. It is checked together with `firstName`, and a pair the portal does not
accept as a name answers 400.

department.description:
The groups to put the new account into, by group ID. Read the IDs from `GET api/2.0/group`; an ID that
matches no group is skipped without an error.

location.description: The free-text location shown on the profile. It is stored as it is given and is not validated.

comment.description: The free-text note kept with the profile, shown to administrators. It is stored as it is given.

contacts.description:
The additional ways to reach the person, each as a type and a value pair. The type is a free-text label such
as `email`, `phone`, `skype` or `telegram`, and an entry with an empty value is dropped.

files.description:
The address the portal downloads the avatar from. It has to use HTTPS unless the request itself came over
HTTP, an address the portal refuses to fetch is rejected, and passing the default avatar path means no
avatar is downloaded.

fromInviteLink.description:
Set it to true when the account is created by somebody accepting an invitation, which makes `key` required
and lets the link decide the type. With the default false the caller has to hold the permission to add an
account of the requested type.

key.description:
The key of the invitation link being accepted, taken from the link itself. It is read only when
`fromInviteLink` is true, and an expired or already used key answers 403.

cultureName.description:
The interface language of the new account, as a culture code. It is applied whether or not the portal has
that culture enabled, so send a code the portal supports.

target.description:
Not used. The handler reads nothing from this field, and it is kept only so that existing clients keep
working.

spam.description:
Whether the account agrees to receive tips, updates and offers. It defaults to false, which means no such
mail is sent.

members.description:
The accounts the operation applies to. When adding or replacing members, an account that is a guest, is
disabled or does not exist is skipped without an error; when removing them, an ID that is not a member is
skipped as well.

name.description:
The new label of the key, up to 30 characters, neither empty nor made of whitespace only. Omit it to keep the
current name.

permissions.description:
The scopes that replace the current ones. Every value has to come from `GET api/2.0/keys/permissions`, an
unknown value or an empty array is rejected, and omitting the field keeps the current scopes.

isActive.description:
Whether the key may authenticate requests. Set it to false to stop the key without deleting it and to true to
let it work again; omit it to keep the current state.

UpdateApiKeyRequest.description: The request parameters for updating an existing API key.

membersToAdd.description:
The accounts to add to the group. An account that is a guest, is disabled or does not exist is skipped
without an error, so the answer has to be read to see what was applied.

membersToRemove.description:
The accounts to remove from the group. Removals are applied after the additions, so an account named in both
lists ends up removed, and an ID that is not a member is skipped without an error.

groupManager.description:
The account to make the manager of the group, which also adds it to the group. Omit it to keep the current
manager - it cannot be cleared through this operation.

groupName.description: The new name of the group, up to 128 characters. Omit it to keep the current name.

UpdateGroupRequest.description: The request for updating a group.

cultureName.description: The user culture name (en-US, de, fr, es, ...).

userId.description:
The account the change applies to. It is read from this body by `POST api/2.0/people/email`, while
`PUT api/2.0/people/{userId}` takes the account from the route and ignores this field.

disable.description:
Set it to true to give the account the `Terminated` status and end every session it has, and to false to
bring it back. It is applied only when the caller edits somebody else, and omitting it keeps the current
status.

isUser.description:
Set it to true to turn the account into a guest and to false to turn it back into a member. Either direction
takes a seat and can answer 402, it is applied only when the caller edits somebody else, and a request to
make the portal owner, a DocSpace administrator or a module administrator a guest is ignored.

firstName.description:
The new first name, up to 255 characters. It is applied only to the caller's own profile, is left alone on an
LDAP or SSO account, and a pair the portal does not accept as a name answers 400.

lastName.description:
The new last name, up to 255 characters. It is applied only to the caller's own profile, is left alone on an
LDAP or SSO account, and a pair the portal does not accept as a name answers 400.

department.description:
The groups the profile should belong to, by group ID, replacing the current ones. It is applied only to the
caller's own profile.

location.description:
The new free-text location shown on the profile. It is applied only to the caller's own profile and is left
alone on an LDAP or SSO account.

comment.description: The new free-text note kept with the profile. It is applied only to the caller's own profile.

contacts.description:
The additional ways to reach the person, replacing the current ones. Each entry is a free-text type such as
`email`, `phone`, `skype` or `telegram` and its value, an entry with an empty value is dropped, and the field
is applied only to the caller's own profile.

files.description:
The address the portal downloads the new avatar from. It is applied only to the caller's own profile, has to
use HTTPS unless the request itself came over HTTP, and passing the address the profile already uses
downloads nothing.

spam.description:
Whether the account agrees to receive tips, updates and offers. It is applied only to the caller's own
profile, and omitting it on such a request stores false rather than keeping the current value.

userIds.description: The accounts the operation applies to. System accounts are dropped from the list without an error.

quota.description:
The personal storage limit in bytes, as a whole number. A value of 0 or more becomes the limit, and any
negative value switches the personal limit off so that the portal default applies again. It is read only by
`PUT api/2.0/people/userquota`.

UpdateMembersQuotaRequestDto.description: The request parameters for updating a user quota.

userIds.description:
The accounts the operation applies to. System accounts are dropped from the list without an error, and the
remaining ones are processed in the order they are given.

resendAll.description:
Reaches every pending account of the portal instead of the ones in `userIds`. It is read only by
`PUT api/2.0/people/invite` and is ignored by every other operation that binds this body.

UpdateMembersRequestDto.description: The request parameters for updating the user information.

files.description:
The address the portal downloads the new avatar from. It has to be absolute or relative to the portal, and it
has to use HTTPS unless the request itself came over HTTP; an address the portal refuses to fetch is rejected.
It is required - an empty value is answered with 400 rather than clearing the avatar.

id.description:
The service limit ID, used to read, change, switch off or delete the limit through the
`api/2.0/portal/payment/servicelimit` operations. For the limit for every user it is the same for all users.

scope.description: Whether the limit is the user's own (`Custom`) or the limit for every user (`Global`) the user falls back to.

amountValue.description:
The most money the AI services may cost the user per period, in `currency`. It is the only threshold a limit on
the AI services has: their services count in different units, so a threshold on a quantity is refused for them.

amountConsumed.description:
The money the AI services cost the user in the current period, in `currency`; 0 when nothing was spent yet,
including a user who has never used the AI services.

currency.description: The currency `amountValue` and `amountConsumed` are expressed in; null when the limit has no money threshold.

period.description:
The window the threshold applies to. It resets at the start of the next day, week or month in UTC (a week on
Monday), not a fixed time after the first charge; a lifetime limit never resets.

periodEnd.description:
The moment the current period ends and the spending starts over from zero, in UTC. Null for a lifetime limit,
which never resets.

UserServiceLimitDto.description:
The spending limit on the AI services in force for one user: the user's personal limit, or else the limit for every
user, together with the money the user spent against it in the current period.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Sliding window rate limit: 1500 requests per minute per user/IP.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Number of requests remaining in the current sliding window (1500 req/min). Concurrent limits also apply: 50 parallel GET requests, 15 parallel POST/PUT requests.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the current sliding window rate limit resets.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Up to 60s for the sliding window (1500 req/min), up to 86400s for the daily POST/PUT limit (10000/day).

Bearer.description: Enter 'Bearer {JWT Token}'. Tokens are validated per RFC8725 (JSON Web Token Best Current Practices): signatures are required and checked against a server-side algorithm allow-list (ES256, RS256) rather than the token header, and issuer, audience and expiry are all verified.

ApiKeyBearer.description: Authentication is determined by the 'Authorization' header
ApiKeyBearer.name: ApiKeyBearer

OAuth2.description: OAuth2 flow with Authorization Code. The access tokens it issues are JWTs, validated per RFC8725 exactly as the Bearer scheme describes.
